title: Assignment convergence
subtitle: Relative flow-change norm per iteration
support_notes: REAL full trace from oct12_run1_40h (completed 2026-10-14, 36h23m): assigned_fraction climbs 3.11% (iter1) -> 4.33 -> 5.14 -> ... -> 11.24% (iter18), hit max_iterations with 63.1M extra isolated flows still outstanding. Increments shrink only gradually (iter2 +1.22%, iter10 +1.11%, iter18 +0.24%) -- near-linear, not sharply decelerating toward an asymptote. Root cause identified: assignment runs in undamped remain_assign_mode=full (default), which re-routes 100% of remaining demand onto the same shortest paths every iteration with no step-size decay -- the classic non-convergent pattern for successive assignment without averaging. The codebase already has an MSA-damped mode (remain_assign_mode=msa, alpha=1/iteration) that is the standard fix, currently unused (opt-in only). Recommendation: validate MSA mode on a short run before committing further Anvil/Hopper compute to more full-mode iterations.

title: Capacity violation check
support_notes: REAL run against oct12_run1_40h (18-iter, 11.24% assigned): 3.01% of links over capacity nationally. By tier: freeway 5.36%, local_access 0.59%, arterial 0.50%, collector 0.46% -- freeway has the HIGHEST over-capacity rate despite holding the largest pool of aggregate spare capacity (27.9B of 63.0B veh/day total), consistent with freight concentrating onto preferred corridors. 78.75% of links have v/c<1%; 56.82% carry zero flow. Finding: this is a concentration/distribution problem, not an aggregate capacity shortage -- total network capacity (63.0B veh/day) is ~886x total national demand (71.1M veh/day).
